question: How many AIS-visible commercial ship crossings of the Strait of Hormuz will hormuz.now record for 26 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the last 27 complete hormuz.now archive days (range 4-13, median 6, mean ~7.6, IQR 5-9.5). Status quo: severe restrictions, mine strikes on 14 Nov, unauthorised tankers turned back, so I shade slightly down; the two weeks to 15 Nov averaged ~7 a day versus ~8 in late October. Upside tail: Iran's two-day reopening proposal and Qatar mediation, the only mechanism for >30 (priced at 2%). Downside tail: severe escalation could give 0-2. Archive figures get revised: 11 Nov now reads 13 although the question background said it showed 4. Markets: no market prices this daily count; the nearest Polymarket contract (PortWatch 7-day average >=60 by 30 Nov) shows 13-16% Yes per search snippets, and Straits.live cites ~1% for reopening by 30 Nov. Different source, threshold and target, so these inform the upside tail only and are not an anchor.

calls.reasoning: Base rate: hormuz.now's own complete daily totals for 20 Oct-15 Nov: median 6, mean ~7.6, range 4-13, right-skewed with occasional 11-13 days; the last fortnight's median was also 6. Mine strikes and tanker fires on 12-14 Nov did not visibly dent the counts (5-6/day). Status quo is a continued restricted-passage regime: Iran-US talks via Qatar are stalled and no reopening date is announced. Left tail widened for the 36h-snapshot undercount risk (11 Nov was later revised from 4 to 13) and for escalation days. The >30 escape needs a reopening deal by 26 Nov; I price it at 2%. No market prices this count; normalization markets settle on PortWatch, so they are not an anchor.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs report the same hormuz.now CSV series and the same revision evidence (the 11 Nov archive page read 4 in the background, 13 now), so there was no factual conflict to settle. The only differences were judgment: the reopening tail (2-4%) and how much snapshot-undercount weight to add on the left. I carry forward the shared reference class and an empirical-spread dispersion of ~9. I chose the low end of the reopening tail given stalled diplomacy and no announced date. I retrieved nothing myself (no web access on this run).
